title: GraphQL query-cost limits: count fields and aliases inside inline fragments and fragment spreads at their parent level
answers: Why does a GraphQL request with fields inside `... on Query` get rejected for exceeding the root fields limit?
Why does MLFLOW_SERVER_GRAPHQL_MAX_ALIASES not catch aliases placed in named fragments?
Where is the GraphQL max depth and total selections limit enforced for incoming queries?
Why are fields in an unused GraphQL fragment not counted toward the query limits?
body:
Path: Incoming GraphQL requests to the MLflow server pass through mlflow/server/graphql/graphql_no_batching.py:scan_query (called via check_query_safety), which enforces MLFLOW_SERVER_GRAPHQL_MAX_ROOT_FIELDS, MLFLOW_SERVER_GRAPHQL_MAX_ALIASES, the max depth and the max total selections on each operation's selection sets.
Rule: Expand InlineFragmentNode and FragmentSpreadNode selections into their parent level before counting, using graphql_no_batching.py:_collect_fields_and_aliases. Fragment definitions are looked up from the document by name, so a spread's fields count as if written inline. Sum aliases across all sibling fragments at a level into one count (scan_query takes the max per level), so aliases cannot be split across fragments to stay under the limit.
Rule: Guard fragment expansion against cycles with a per-path visited set (visited_fragments frozenset passed down the stack in scan_query; local_visited in _collect_fields_and_aliases). Fragment-expanded fields still increment total_selections and are subject to _MAX_SELECTIONS.
Symptom: A query with more root fields or aliases than the configured limit, written with `... on Query { ... }` or with `...FragmentName` spreads, was executed by the server instead of being rejected with 'exceeds maximum root fields' / 'exceeds maximum aliases'.
Constraints: Only OperationDefinitionNode definitions are scanned; fragment definitions are counted only when reached by a spread from an operation, so unused fragments do not count. Do not propagate local_visited into child depths: a fragment reused at two depths (diamond) must still be counted at both. Termination for cycles is also guaranteed by the depth and total-selection caps.
applies: Applies to the GraphQL query-cost scanner in the MLflow server; does not cover the GraphQL resolvers or per-field authorization.
says: GraphQL request with fields inside a fragment gets rejected for exceeding the root fields limit
Aliases placed in a named GraphQL fragment are not caught by the server's alias limit
Fragment fields escape the server's query depth and selection count checks
Unused GraphQL fragments are ignored by the server's query limits
Server should count fields and aliases from inline fragments and fragment spreads toward the query limits
search: GraphQL query-cost limits in the MLflow server: fields and aliases reached through inline fragments and fragment spreads are counted at their parent level, with cycle guarding. Only operations are scanned, so unused fragments do not count. Fragment-expanded fields still count toward the total selections cap.
